diagnostic_evidence.quote: For all other tuples $f$, we have $\deg X>r$ and there exist linear space of projective dimension $r-1$ that intersects $X$ in more than $r$ real points

issues.failure_explanation: The Bézout argument giving r = n_codim^f + 1 applies exactly when deg X = codim X + 1, i.e. when X is a variety of minimal degree. Segre–Veronese varieties of minimal degree include not only P^1 x P^{b} (the case listed) but also rational normal curves nu_d(P^1) (a single nonzero f_i = d with m_i = 2), the Veronese surface nu_2(P^2) (single nonzero f_i = 2, m_i = 3), and P^1 x P^1 embedded by O(1,b). For these the assertion deg X > r is false and the span of r = n_codim^f + 1 generic rank-one tensors meets X in exactly those r points, so uniqueness holds. Concretely for f = (2,0) on S^2(R^2) ⊗ R^k the theorem gives r(f) = min{n_col, 1} = 1, yet any 2-dimensional span of two rank-one symmetric 2x2 matrices contains exactly those two (a line meets a conic in 2 points), as the paper's own Example ex:two exhibits; for f = (2) on S^2(R^3), 4 generic rank-one symmetric matrices span a P^3 meeting the Veronese surface in exactly 4 points, so r(f) = 4, not 3.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the special case by 'X is a Segre–Veronese variety of minimal degree' (rational normal scrolls P^1 x P^b with O(1,1), P^1 x P^1 with O(1,b), rational normal curves nu_d(P^1), the Veronese surface nu_2(P^2)), and restrict the citation of ranestad2024real to the non-minimal-degree cases.
issues.overall_effect: The stated 'largest r' formula is wrong (under-counts by one) for a family of flattenings, and the proof's claim of an open set of non-unique decompositions for r = n_codim^f + 1 is false there; the formulas in Corollary r_max with matching inherit the error in those cases.
issues.title: r(f) formula misses all Segre–Veronese varieties of minimal degree (case split incomplete)
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false as stated in identifiable cases and the case analysis must be redone via the classification of minimal-degree varieties, but the corrected statement is of the same form and the algorithmic use of r(f) survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof adapts \cite[Theorem~2.3]{schneider2015convergence} to blockwise updates.

issues.failure_explanation: Inequality (eq: lojasiewicz) is stated for the block restriction F_i with the other blocks fixed, with constants theta_i, Lambda_i, sigma; but F_i depends on the current values of the other blocks, which change along the iteration, so uniform constants are not justified, and F_i(v_*^{(i)}) with the other blocks at their current values is not F(v_*). The proof nevertheless substitutes F(v_*) - F(v_{(k,i)}) on the left-hand side and the block Riemannian gradient ||∇_S F_i(v_{(k,i)})|| on the right. The needed inequality is a Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz inequality for the full F on the product of spheres, whose right-hand side is the full gradient; relating the full gradient to the block gradients at intermediate points (via Lipschitz continuity and the fact that the just-updated block has small gradient) is a nontrivial step of block-coordinate KL analyses and is absent. Also the step from 2Λ(G-G')/G^θ to 2Λ(G^{1-θ}-G'^{1-θ}) drops the factor 1/(1-θ).

failure_location.quote: Then equation \eqref{eq: lojasiewicz} holds for $\fv_{(k,i)}$ and together with \eqref{eq:function_increase}, we obtain

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reprove convergence with a KL inequality for F on the full product manifold plus a relative-error bound ||∇F(v_{(k+1,1)})|| ≤ C Σ_i ||v^{(i,k+1)} - v^{(i,k)}|| obtained from Lipschitz gradients (block-coordinate KL framework), and a sufficient-decrease bound requiring ||∇F_i|| bounded below (e.g. τ_0 + γ_i > 0), restoring the constant 1/(1-θ).
issues.overall_effect: Global convergence of PS-HOPM iterates (and the algebraic rate) is not established as written; Proposition shift for Ttilde A relies on this theorem.
issues.title: Global convergence proof misapplies the Łojasiewicz inequality to single-block restrictions
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is plausible and the repair follows a known but nontrivial block-coordinate KL argument that must be supplied; no result is lost but a contained new argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: convex in each block. Global convergence of Algorithm~\ref{alg:psspm} then follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:power_method_convergence}.

issues.failure_explanation: h is decreasing with h(1)=0, and F_A ≤ 1 always, so under the literal hypothesis 'F ≤ ν' one may take ν = 1 and obtain γ_i = 0 for all f_i > 1; but the block restriction of F_A need not be convex then (e.g. A = span{diag(1,-1)/√2} gives F_A(x) = (x_1^2 - x_2^2)^2/2, not convex), so the proposition as stated is false. Moreover F as written already contains the shift terms, making the hypothesis circular. The intended reading (ν a lower bound on the function value along the iteration, as in the SPM adaptive shift) yields a Hessian bound only at points with F_A ≥ ν, whereas the invoked Theorem power_method_convergence requires convexity of each block restriction over all of R^{m_i}; the proof does not bridge this gap.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State ν as a lower bound on F_A at the initial (hence all) iterates, define F without the shift terms in the hypothesis, and prove the monotonic increase/convergence argument using convexity only on the region where F_A ≥ ν (or on the relevant segments), adapting the SPM argument explicitly.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised smaller shifts (< 1) for T-tilde are not justified; global convergence with these shifts is unsupported.
issues.title: Shift condition for T-tilde stated with reversed/circular hypothesis and no global convexity
issues.why_classification: The statement must be corrected and a contained argument added to replace the appeal to global convexity; the qualitative result (shifts below 1 suffice) can plausibly be retained.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: has local linear convergence around every pSVT that is a second-order critical point of $F$ with positive singular value
by \eqref{eq:beta12mu} and the negative definiteness of the Hessian of $F$.

issues.failure_explanation: A second-order critical point only has a negative semidefinite Riemannian Hessian. With semidefiniteness the argument yields λ ≤ 1 rather than λ < 1 (equality possible along a null direction of the Hessian, e.g. T = I_2 has a circle of maximizers and the Jacobian has eigenvalue 1 along it), so the spectral radius bound and hence linear convergence fail at degenerate maximizers. The proof also writes (eq: lambda mu) as if ||v|| = ||w|| = 1 while using ||v||^2 + ||w||^2 = 1 for β_1 + β_2 ≤ 1, and asserts β_1 + β_2 = 1 in the μ = 0 case without justification; the argument goes through only after inserting the norms ||v||^2, ||w||^2 and using strict negativity.

failure_location.quote: since $\mathbf{H}_{1,1}$ is negative definite, being a submatrix of the Hessian at a maximizer.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that the Riemannian Hessian of F at the pSVT is negative definite (nondegenerate maximizer) and correct the normalization in (eq: lambda mu).
issues.overall_effect: Local linear convergence is established only at nondegenerate (strict) local maximizers, not at every second-order critical point as stated.
issues.title: Local linear convergence assumes negative definite Hessian, but only second-order criticality is hypothesized
issues.why_classification: A standard local nondegeneracy hypothesis and a routine normalization fix restore the result with the same method and conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: From ⟨T_w,R^(i)⟩ = μ_i + Σ_{j≠i} μ_j ⟨R^(j),R^(i)⟩ one only gets |μ_i - ⟨R^(i),T_w⟩| ≤ (r-1)ρ ||μ||_∞, not ρ||μ||_∞; hence ||μ||_∞ ≤ max|⟨R^(i),T_w⟩|/(1-(r-1)ρ), which requires (r-1)ρ < 1 (not assumed). The stated bound fails: for ℓ=1, f=1, r=3 vectors v_1=e_1, v_2=(cos60°,sin60°,0), v_3 ≈ (cos60°,-sin60°cosφ, sin60° sinφ) with small φ, ρ ≈ 1/2, A = R^3 so F_A(e_3)=1, but C·max_i|⟨v_i,e_3⟩| ≈ 4·0.87φ < 1. Additionally, the step Σ|⟨v_i,w⟩|^{ℓ f_j} ≤ Σ|⟨v_i,w⟩|^2 is invalid when f_j = 0 (the sum equals r), so the product over k in C should range only over k with f_k > 0 with exponent 1/#{f_k>0}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (1-ρ)^{-1} by (1-(r-1)ρ)^{-1}, add the hypothesis (r-1)ρ < 1, and restrict the Hölder/Gershgorin product to indices with f_k > 0 (exponent 1/#{f_k>0}).
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative statement that non-optimal critical points of F_A have low objective value is not established with the stated constant; it holds only under (r-1)ρ < 1 with a larger constant.
issues.title: Upper bound on F_A uses wrong constant (missing factor r-1) and is false without (r-1)ρ < 1
issues.why_classification: The correction weakens the bound and adds a genuine hypothesis excluding the regime (r-1)ρ ≥ 1, but a recognizably comparable estimate survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\min(f,f')\neq 0$ means $\nexists i$ such that $f_i = f'_i = 0$
If \(\min(f,f')>0\), recovery is complete. Otherwise, use the shared factors between $d-f$ and $f'$ to find the remaining factors.

issues.failure_explanation: Step 2 needs a shared index (some i with f_i, f'_i > 0), i.e. min(f,f') is not the zero vector; the text instead defines min(f,f') ≠ 0 as 'no index with f_i = f'_i = 0', which is a different (entrywise positivity) condition. Recovery after steps 1–2 is complete iff every index appears in f or f', i.e. max(f,f') > 0 entrywise; the algorithm tests min(f,f') > 0, which under the text's definition is always true and would skip the necessary third step in the paper's own example (f=(1,1,0,0), f'=(1,0,1,0), where index 4 is unrecovered). Corollary r_max with matching (3) uses the same wrong case condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the requirement as ∃ i with f_i, f'_i > 0, and replace the completeness test min(f,f') > 0 by max(f,f') > 0 entrywise in the algorithm, prose, and Corollary (3).
issues.overall_effect: The branching of the completion procedure and the case split in Corollary r_max with matching (3) are incorrect as written; the intended procedure (as in the figure) is recoverable.
issues.title: Non-symmetry-breaking recovery conditions garbled (min vs max, wrong definition of min(f,f')≠0)
issues.why_classification: Local corrections of the conditions restore the intended procedure and formulas without loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the vectors $\fv_{i}^{(j)}$ are generic with norm one, and assume $\dim \Acal = r$.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement assumes only genericity and dim A = r, but the uniqueness conclusion requires that A = span{R^(i)_(d)} contain no rank-one tensors other than the R^(i)_(d), which holds only when r ≤ n_codim for the full Segre–Veronese variety in ⊗S^{d_j} (i.e. r ≤ r(d) in the theorem's notation). The proof invokes 'r ≤ r(f)', which is neither a hypothesis nor the relevant quantity (A is spanned by the R^(i)_(d), not the R^(i)_(f)). For r exceeding this bound A contains infinitely many rank-one tensors and the claimed uniqueness can fail.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, the $r$ rank-one tensors $\{\mathscr{R}^{(i)}_{(f)}\}_{i=1}^r$ are the only rank-one elements in $\Acal$ (up to scale), since $r \leq r(f)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis r ≤ r(d) (in the theorem's notation; r ≤ r(d-f) in its application) and cite Theorem rmax_formula for the uniqueness of rank-one elements of A.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem match up patterns is unsupported for large r; Corollary r_max with matching already imposes r ≤ r(d-f), consistent with the needed hypothesis.
issues.title: Factor-matching theorem lacks the rank hypothesis its proof uses
issues.why_classification: Adding the omitted, already-used hypothesis fixes the statement; downstream usage already assumes it.

issues.failure_explanation: The deflated matrix is U D V^T with D = C^{-1} - a_u a_v^T/(a_v^T C a_u). D annihilates C a_u (so the row space is span{C a_u}^⊥, matching O_u), but its column space is span{C^T a_v}^⊥, not span{C a_v}^⊥. Example: U=V=I_2, C=[[1,1],[0,1]], a_u=a_v=e_1 gives deflated matrix [[0,-1],[0,1]] with column space span{(-1,1)}, while the paper's O_v = e_2 yields Û = e_2 and Û Ĉ^{-1} V̂^T = e_2 e_2^T ≠ deflated matrix, so (b) and (c) fail. After the first deflation Ĉ = O_u^T C O_v is generally non-symmetric, so Algorithm MSPM's deflation is incorrect from the second component onward as written (the algorithm also never sets C ← D^{-1}).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define O_v as an orthonormal basis of span{C^T a_v}^⊥ in the proposition and algorithm, and initialize C ← D^{-1} after the SVD.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition deflation (2)(b),(c) and the Deflation step of Algorithm MSPM produce a wrong subspace whenever C is non-symmetric, i.e. after the first deflation.
issues.title: Deflation basis uses C a_v instead of C^T a_v; fails once C is non-symmetric
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol local correction (transpose) restores all claims with no loss of content.
